page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an entry-level compute-focused virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on the x86_64 architecture. The configuration allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs, which correspond to a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled across two execution threads. The underlying processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Memory capacity is configured at 2.0 GB, yielding a 1.0 GB per vCPU ratio. This server includes no integrated local storage and zero GPU accelerators, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent disk storage.

Benchmark measurements indicate solid single-threaded performance paired with low overall multi-threaded throughput due to the single-core execution boundary. In stress-ng evaluation, single-core performance registered at 2684.89, placing it in the top quartile of recorded results, whereas multi-core throughput registered at 2695.68, reflecting bottom-quartile multi-threaded scaling. Geekbench testing mirrors this behavior, producing an average single-core score of 1465.0 alongside a multi-core score of 1813.0. Memory throughput is modest, reaching 29.49 GB/sec in uncached sequential reads and 21.35 GB/sec in sequential writes. Application workloads with elevated memory demands show restrained throughput, exemplified by 1.98 million Redis SET operations per second and 2.41 GB/sec in static web serving.

Qualitatively, the n2d-highcpu-2 offers an economical profile for dedicated execution time on modern AMD hardware without incurring costs for unneeded memory capacity. The primary operational bottleneck is the compact 2.0 GB memory envelope, which limits the instance from hosting memory-intensive applications, heavy databases, or complex multi-tenant containers. The hardware profile is best suited for lightweight compute-bound processing, single-threaded execution tasks, modest CI/CD build scripts, background job queues, and utility microservices with minimal RAM requirements.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-2 is an entry-level compute-oriented virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core of an AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processor. The instance provides 2.0 GB of system memory, matching a 1.0 GB per vCPU density, and incorporates 32 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware acceleration for AES, VAES, and SHA cryptographic operations. It includes no bundled local disks or GPU accelerators, relying on remote persistent storage for disk needs. Benchmark assessments show robust single-core capabilities, achieving top-quartile performance in stress-ng single-core tests, yet overall system throughput is limited by the low core count and narrow memory bandwidth. Uncached read bandwidth peaks at 29.49 GB/sec, while static web serving achieves 2.41 GB/sec. The n2d-highcpu-2 is cost-effective for single-threaded processing that does not require large memory arrays, making it appropriate for lightweight background jobs, basic CI/CD worker agents, small batch scripts, and simple network proxies.
